record.paper_title: Open Problems in Universal Induction & Intelligence
record.original_question: For which restricted environmental classes—such as Markov, factorizable, forgetful, relevant, asymptotically learnable, farsighted, uniform, or pseudo-passive environments—can one define and prove general value bounds or optimality properties for AIXI?

evidence.quote: b) Limited environmental classes. The problem of defining and proving general value bounds becomes more feasible by considering, in a first step, restricted concept classes. One could analyze AIXI for known classes (like Markov or factorizable environments) and especially for the new classes (forgetful, relevant, asymptotically learnable, farsighted, uniform, and (pseudo-)passive) defined in [Hut05].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the universal reinforcement-learning agent AIXI, defined as follows. An environment is a conditional probability measure $\mu(o_{1:n}r_{1:n}\mid a_{1:n})$ over sequences of observations $o_t$ and rewards $r_t\in[0,1]$ given a sequence of actions $a_t$ chosen from finite alphabets. For a policy $\pi$, the expected future $\mu$-value at time $k$ with horizon $m$ is 
$$V^\pi_\mu(\ae_{<k}) \;=\; \mathbb{E}_\mu\!\left[\sum_{t=k}^{k+m} r_t \,\Big|\, \ae_{<k},\, a_{k:k+m}\sim\pi\right].$$
The Bayes-optimal AIXI policy with respect to a class $\mathcal{M}$ of environments and prior $w:\mathcal{M}\to(0,1]$ with $\sum_\nu w_\nu \le 1$ is the policy maximizing $V^\pi_\xi$, where $\xi(\,\cdot\,)=\sum_{\nu\in\mathcal{M}} w_\nu\,\nu(\,\cdot\,)$. When $\mathcal{M}$ is the class of all lower semicomputable chronological semimeasures with universal Solomonoff-type prior, this defines AIXI.

Recall the following restricted environment classes:
(i) $n$-Markov: the conditional distribution of $(o_t,r_t)$ given history depends only on the last $n$ action–percept pairs.
(ii) Factorizable: $\mu$ factorizes into independent episodes of bounded length.
(iii) Forgetful: the influence of the initial history on future percepts vanishes uniformly.
(iv) Relevant: only finitely much past information is needed to predict the future to arbitrary accuracy.
(v) Asymptotically learnable: there exists a policy whose predictions converge to the true conditional in $\mu$-probability.
(vi) Farsighted: the limit $\lim_{m\to\infty} V^\pi_\mu$ exists for the relevant policies.
(vii) Uniform: the per-step rewards have a structure that is uniform across histories.
(viii) Pseudo-passive (and passive): the agent's actions do not influence (resp. only weakly influence) future percepts.

Problem. For each of the above restricted classes $\mathcal{C}$, determine whether one can prove a nontrivial general value bound or optimality property for the Bayes-optimal AIXI policy $\pi^\xi$ relative to the best informed policy $\pi^\mu$, of the form
$$V^{\pi^\xi}_\mu - V^{\pi^\mu}_\mu \longrightarrow 0 \quad \text{(in some appropriate sense)}$$
uniformly or $\mu$-almost surely for every $\mu\in\mathcal{C}$, and identify the largest such class for which a meaningful bound or optimality theorem can be established.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial progress exists. Hutter's 2005 monograph and follow-up work establish self-optimizingness of Bayes-optimal agents on classes such as ergodic MDPs, factorizable, forgetful, relevant, (pseudo-)passive and asymptotically learnable environments, and Leike's 2016 thesis "Nonparametric General Reinforcement Learning" extends asymptotic optimality results in mean and Cesàro senses for restricted classes. However, fully general value bounds or strong optimality properties for AIXI itself across all of these classes (especially uniform and farsighted) remain incomplete; recent work (e.g., 2025 "Value Under Ignorance in Universal Artificial Intelligence") continues to refine the picture, indicating the question is partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Nonparametric General Reinforcement Learning (Leike, 2016)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops asymptotic optimality results for Bayesian agents on restricted classes of environments, refining and extending Hutter's framework.
status_evidence.claim: Asymptotic optimality / value-bound results for AIXI-like agents have been established on several restricted environment classes.

status_evidence.title: Value Under Ignorance in Universal Artificial Intelligence (2025)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent analysis of value bounds for universal agents under various environment-class assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Work on value bounds for AIXI under restricted environment classes is ongoing as of 2025.

status_evidence.title: AIXI Technical Report (Hutter)
status_evidence.snippet: Defines and analyzes AIXI for Markov, factorizable, forgetful, relevant, asymptotically learnable, farsighted, uniform, and (pseudo-)passive environments.
status_evidence.claim: Restricted environment classes are defined and partial value/optimality results are given, but a complete characterization is left open.
